builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: FOREST: Coordinating Tree-based HBF, RRAM, and HBM for Efficient Speculative LLM Inference
summary: FOREST replaces GPU-centric speculative decoding, where drafting, target verification, and KV-cache attention all share HBM and general-purpose compute, with a heterogeneous memory-centric architecture coordinating HBF, 3D-stacked RRAM, and HBM compute trees, including BFP attention and pipelined softmax. The cost is that it is a hardware architecture proposal requiring non-existent custom silicon (RRAM crossbars, HBF stacks, clock-decoupled interfaces), plus numerical co-design that depends on block-floating-point quantization of attention, which can degrade model quality. It can fail through RRAM device non-idealities and endurance limits, unproven manufacturability, simulation-based rather than measured results, and the fact that none of it is deployable on the reader's GPU or API infrastructure.
rationale: The method requires custom HBF, 3D-stacked RRAM, and HBM memory-compute hardware that does not exist as a purchasable product, so the reader can only track it while continuing to use GPU-based speculative decoding, which already works on a single 24 GB card.
technique: Heterogeneous HBF-RRAM-HBM hardware for speculative decoding

claims.statement: FOREST replaces GPU-centric speculative decoding, where drafting, target verification, and KV-cache attention all share HBM and general-purpose compute, with a heterogeneous memory-centric architecture coordinating HBF, 3D-stacked RRAM, and HBM compute trees, including BFP attention and pipelined softmax. The cost is that it is a hardware architecture proposal requiring non-existent custom silicon (RRAM crossbars, HBF stacks, clock-decoupled interfaces), plus numerical co-design that depends on block-floating-point quantization of attention, which can degrade model quality. It can fail through RRAM device non-idealities and endurance limits, unproven manufacturability, simulation-based rather than measured results, and the fact that none of it is deployable on the reader's GPU or API infrastructure.

Up to 5.5x end-to-end speedup, 11.46x higher decode throughput, 16.5x higher decode energy efficiency, and up to 6.73x higher token-generation cost efficiency over NVIDIA A800 GPU-based speculative decoding baselines, evaluated on 32B-405B target models.
